question: Does one sealed genome of a few hundred bytes grow, on each device’s own data and offline, an organism that answers only where it has earned it — and refuse to grow at all when a single byte is changed?

substrates.reference: all four domains as seed-library sealed them
substrates.device-a: the same four domains, holding only the even half of each train history
substrates.shuffled-shopper: shopper labels shuffled (seed 9) so there is nothing left to learn; the other domains as the reference

rules.claim: the whole four-organ genome, sealed, is at most 512 bytes
rules.seenBeforeSeal: yes — 496 bytes in a smoke run and a unit test

rules.claim: all five germinations, the seal check included, make no network call
rules.seenBeforeSeal: yes — for the reference germination, in a unit test

rules.claim: on the reference data every organ reproduces seed-library’s sealed held-out AUC exactly, and answers every held case at exactly the accuracy the ribosome grades
rules.seenBeforeSeal: yes — in a smoke run and the unit tests

rules.claim: every one-character change to the genome is refused; the maker’s key swapped is refused on the signature; another maker’s trust list refuses it
rules.seenBeforeSeal: yes — the unit tests run the same sweep

rules.claim: the rules it grows are at least twice the bytes the genome carries: the device’s data supplies the rest
on device-a and device-b, each holding half the history, all four organs still clear the gate, each within 0.03 AUC of the reference, and the three organisms all differ
rules.seenBeforeSeal: partly — a unit test saw the two ids differ and at least one organ’s rules differ; no device-shard state or AUC has been looked at

rules.claim: germination is deterministic: three more runs grow the reference organism’s id, and CI re-derives the record byte for byte
rules.seenBeforeSeal: yes — in a unit test, locally

rules.claim: with the shopper labels shuffled the shopper organ scores a coin (held-out AUC from 0.45 to 0.55), is cut, and abstains on every shopper case, while the other three organs answer every case
rules.seenBeforeSeal: partly — a unit test saw it cut with AUC under 0.6; the AUC itself and the other organs’ calls have not been looked at

rules.claim: with no water data the water organ is dormant and abstains on every water case; the other three are live and answer every case

disclosure: This organ was built and unit-tested before this seal, so most rules were seen first and are properties the build claims, not predictions. Only R6 (half the history is enough, within 0.03) and R8 (no signal reads as a coin, and cutting one organ leaves the rest whole) are unseen in the part that matters. A failed prediction is kept in the verdict, not re-run until it passes.
judgedBy: tools/judge.mjs (pinned below): a rule it does not know is a FAIL
